* Estimated — hourly median derived from annual median ÷ 2,080 hrs, applied identically to national and metro-area figures. BLS does not publish an hourly figure for these cases.

Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025 estimates (bls.gov/oes), covering national and metropolitan-area detailed occupations. Figures cover wage-and-salary workers (W-2 employees); self-employed and unincorporated business owners are excluded. An asterisk / “—” indicates a value suppressed by BLS for reliability or confidentiality. Annual wages are calculated by BLS as the hourly mean wage × 2,080 hours for occupations where annual figures are not directly collected. Where BLS publishes an annual median but no hourly median, the hourly median shown here is derived as the annual median ÷ 2,080 hours and flagged with an asterisk; this derivation is applied identically to national and metro-area figures and is never substituted for a value BLS itself suppressed. How this was built and checked: this tool was produced through a human-directed, AI-assisted process. An editor set the structure and reviewed the work at each stage; an AI assistant did the heavy lifting of restructuring the BLS all_data_M_2025 release into the interactive format shown here, with no intermediate calculations or transformations. The result was then independently reconciled, in a separate AI-assisted pass working from the original BLS source file, alongside the editor's own manual spot-checks. That reconciliation compared every line item — all 830 national occupations and 141,015 metropolitan occupation cells across 393 metro areas, roughly 1.1 million individual values covering employment, mean and median wages, and every published percentile — against the BLS file, in both directions, confirming an exact match with no missing, extra, altered, or fabricated values. Each BLS suppression flag was verified to render as a blank, and each blank to correspond to a genuine suppression. Derived hourly medians (7,824 cells, marked with an asterisk) were separately checked to equal the annual median ÷ 2,080 and to appear only where BLS published an annual figure but no hourly one. The automated reconciliation is a value-by-value comparison and not a substitute for the source itself; the underlying BLS file should be treated as the authoritative reference.
